weather_notes: Farm newly acquired; trees not yet bearing.

First recorded harvest year. Source: Delta Packing Co. of Lodi 'Crop Insurance Worksheet Summary' + grower settlement statements (Lot 59) -- exact figures, not an estimate. Bing sold at $1.60/lb, Brook (Brooks) at $1.56/lb. Matches the crop-insurance production report's 30,514 total exactly. Bloom reported Jan 2024, unusually early for Central Valley sweet cherry (normally ~March) -- but 2024 was a documented record-warm winter/early-bloom year statewide for CA cherries, so this is plausible, not a misremembered date.

Good yield reported by grower but exact figure/dates NEEDS INPUT -- not found in the photographed document set (which only covered the 2024 packing/insurance season plus input-cost invoices through early 2025). Likely exists in a 2025 packing settlement statement not yet photographed.

Confirmed 0 yield. Cause reported as likely weather: untimely frost and/or untimely hot weather (exact timing/which-one NEEDS INPUT). Both are literature-supported cherry yield killers at specific phenology windows -- frost during bloom, heat >=91-99F near ripening/harvest -- so once real 2026 CIMIS data is pulled, checking for a cold snap during the bloom window and a heat spell near harvest is the first thing to test against this. This is the most valuable data point in the set: a total crop failure right after two successful years (2024, 2025) is the clearest possible driver-analysis contrast.
